label: Central Texas — Austin, the Blackland Prairie and the eastern Hill Country
why: A list of what a person can actually pick up at an Austin nursery, with the fields lib/design.py and lib/niches.py read. It holds plant facts only, so it carries no address and belongs to no yard.

sources.name: City of Austin Grow Green — Native and Adapted Landscape Plants, an Earth-Wise Guide for Central Texas
sources.note: The list Austin nurseries stock and label against. Primary source for light, water and mature size.

sources.name: Lady Bird Johnson Wildflower Center Native Plant Database
sources.note: Primary source for natives: soil reaction, bloom months and habit.

sources.name: Texas A&M AgriLife Extension — Earth-Kind Landscaping and the Texas Superstar programme
sources.note: Source for adapted non-natives and for the vegetable and herb records.

sources.name: Grown widely in Austin gardens on alkaline soil
sources.note: Used only to widen a pH upper bound, never to set the rest of a record. Any record leaning on this carries a ph_note saying so.

seasons.why: The months a plant is in active growth and needs light. lib/fits.py expands this into the `months` list that design.zone_hours averages over, so the light question is asked over the right window. Not the same as `bloom`. A record may override with an explicit `months` list.

rooting_depth_note: Inches to the bottom of the feeding root zone, by growth-form class, not by species measurement. design.rooting_depth reads it and design.ph_by_layer uses it to decide which soil layers a plant is judged against. The class is named in rooting_depth_source so the figure can be argued with.
